which parked sender's clause the arriving select commits is L1 latitude (which worker parked / arrives first) plus the L2 clause pick on both-parked schedules: certified set {10, 20} (members=2); width 3 caps the computed bounds (|runnable| <= 3, L2 <= 2)

one close waking a width-2 same-channel select does NOT determine the committed clause (the C7 falsified-wording corner): certified set {1, 2} (members=2) — wake head-commit yields 1, the always-realizable close-before-entry schedule + entry L2 draw yields 2; gc exhibits both (~half each, 200-run-per-config probe counts)

which clause a close-woken select commits is L1 wake-timing latitude plus the L2 entry pick on worker-first schedules: certified set {1, 2} (members=2); width 2 caps the computed bounds (scheduler <= 2, L2 <= 2)

THE WEDGE ROW (register #1 discharge): gc's completing execution (42, exit 0; 60/60 observed) is an enumerated member — pre-B1 it was outside the envelope on every stream (the definitional bug); the always-spin schedules stay in the envelope by right (dossier §3.1/§4.3) and are counted as nonterm branches, never members; membership = oracle ∈ TERMINATING set {42} (members=1 under the declared nonterm accounting)

partner progress between wake and abort is B1 postOp + L5 exit-window latitude: certified set {panic "worker abort in the private segment", 42} (members=2, statuses=ok+panic); pre-B1 the panic member was the sole member on every stream — the U-1 class row
the ok/panic split is the main-exit window pick: exit-now discards the woken receiver, any continue schedule reaches its panic; window bound 2, scheduler bound 2
same window at the close-wake boundary (TSan-green: recv is acquire-only at the chan object); ok = exit-now, panic = the woken receiver runs

the three worker sends commit into the cap-3 buffer in scheduler order (L1): the arrival-order code ranges over the 6 permutations of {1,2,3} (members=6); width 4 covers the up-to-4-runnable scheduler bound; no append spill (the results slice is pre-capped at 3); sites raised for the 4-thread tree

the raw created-entry produce-or-skip observable (the strict sibling added-entries-bound normalizes it away): admitted set {1,2} under the ruled full-literal envelope — key 1 is a mandatory never-removed start key, entry 2 is created exactly once and may be produced or skipped. RED under the snapshot machine (enumerated set is the singleton {1} — the dead narrowing made visible); flips green at the (L) surgery. Width bound: pick-next is live candidates + stop, at most 2+1 — width 16 >= 3

the handshake-ordered cross-goroutine delete+re-create of the first-produced key makes it a NEW entry: admitted set {3 (skipped), 4 (produced again)} (members=2); consumption sites are the map pick-next (bound live candidates + stop <= 4) and the L1/postOp scheduler picks (|runnable| <= 2) — width 4 covers both; gc's plain-shape sample is 3 (never 4 in 160k trials), the insert row is where gc exhibits the re-production member

same handshake shape with ONE fresh insert (a created entry, may be produced or skipped) between the delete and the re-create; the observable counts productions of the handed-over key only: admitted set {1 (skipped), 2 (produced again)} (members=2) — gc exhibits BOTH (~87% n=2 at size 3, one insert); pick-next bound <= 4 live candidates + stop = 5, scheduler bound 2 — width 8 >= 5

same-goroutine delete + ONE fresh insert + re-add of the first-produced key (I-1 / L-012: the re-created key is a NEW entry): admitted set {1 (skipped), 2 (produced again)} (members=2) — gc exhibits BOTH (~87% n=2 at the probe), the oracle-exhibited twin of delete-readd-during-range; the only consumption site is the pick-next, bound <= 4 live candidates + stop = 5 — width 8 >= 5

REWORKED from a strict exact-count pin (2026-08-19 ruling: full literal envelope — the old count-3 pin encoded the dead at-most-once-per-key narrowing). A deleted-then-re-created key is a NEW created entry and may be produced again, so the honest claim is membership: gc's sample (3, its only exhibited member, 400/400 probe runs) lies inside the admitted set {3, 4, -1}; -1 is the subject's own truncation of the genuinely unbounded tail, an admitted member. Width bound: the pick-next site's bound is live candidates + the stop slot, at most 3+1 — width 16 >= 4

the composed observable electionTimeout + (first key of a fresh 5-key map range) realizes raft's jitter contract range [5,10): admitted set {5,6,7,8,9} (members=5); the only consumption site is the map pick-next, bound = remaining snapshot size + stop, at most 5+1 — width 16 >= 6

the first key produced by range over a 3-key map observes the map-iteration pick-next choice site; Go randomizes iteration order per run, so repeated samples explore the admitted set {1,2,3}. Width bound: the pick-next site's bound is the remaining snapshot size, at most 3 (then 2, then 1) — width 16 >= 3

the delivery-order draw over a fresh campaign's two vote requests realizes the network-reordering envelope on the twin kernel: admitted set {21, 31} (members=2) — either request may be delivered first and its receiver grants; the only consumption site is the map pick-next over the fresh 2-key pick map (the D-11 idiom); the enumerator's mechanical bound at the pick is 32 — width 40 >= 32

the two children's sends into the cap-2 buffer commit in scheduler order (L1): admitted set {12, 21} (members=2); the consumption sites are the L1 picks over at most 3 runnable goroutines (no append spill: the buffer is pre-sized) — width 4 >= 3
map iteration order over three never-mutated keys: the 6 permutations (members=6, spec: order not specified); consumption is the E9 pick-next over at most 3 live candidates + stop — width 4 >= 4
both clauses are entry-ready: the L2 pick (spec: uniform pseudo-random, weakened possibilistically): admitted set {1, 2} (members=2); the only consumption site is the L2 pick with bound 2

which original key is produced first is the E9 pick (2 orders); if key 1 comes first the created key 9 exists when key 2 is reached and may be produced (before its deletion) or skipped: admitted set {2, 3} (members=2); pick-next bound is live candidates + stop <= 4 — width 4

the store-release/load-acquire pair: on the path where the flag is seen the plain data read is HB-after the plain write (mem#atomic's synchronized-before), on the other path no data read happens — race-free on every path; the SC-excluded stale-data member 100 is absent; admitted {0, 1}
an RMW (Add 0) observing the store inherits the storer's clock (TSan mo_acq_rel; mem#atomic) — the conditional plain read is ordered; admitted {0, 1}

the isolating shape (audit fix H5): the reader spins on CompareAndSwap(&flag,0,0) — success while 0, FAILURE on observing the store — so the loop exit is the failing CAS and its acquire (TSan mo_acquire on failure; mem#atomic: the failed CAS observed the store) is the ONLY edge ordering the plain data read after the plain write; no path refuses; members {5}, the always-spin schedules are nonterm branches (no termination claim)

the two publish/poll goroutines' commit order is L1 latitude: admitted set {1, 10, 11}, 00 SC-forbidden — certified by schedule enumeration with the members=3 cardinality pin; go samples (plain and -race) must be members

gc allocates exactly newLen for 16-byte elements at small sizes (cap 2 for nil []string -> len 2), BELOW the growth formula's max(4,newLen)=4 — the envelope's lower bound is the spec floor newLen. Site bound = max(32, 2*growth) - newLen + 1 = 31; width 32 >= 31

gc size-class rounding realizes cap 224 for []int oldCap 100 -> newLen 101 (formula 200, old window [200,208)) — above the old envelope. Widened envelope [101, max(32, 2*200)=400]; site bound = 400-101+1 = 300; width 300; cap 320 (300 distinct capacities exceed the default 64 observation cap)

gc stack-buffers small non-escaping appends (32-byte buffer): realized cap 32 for a byte append at oldCap 3 -> newLen 4, outside the old growth+[0,8) window. Version-tracks the stack-buffer point against the widened envelope [newLen, max(32, 2*growth)] (site bound = upper-newLen+1 = 29; width 32 >= 29)

cap() after append spills a zero-cap full-slice window, observing the append-capacity choice site (envelope [newLen, max(32, 2*growth)] since the F2 widening, arc-final audit 2026-08-06); Go picks one capacity deterministically per toolchain, so samples=1 version-tracks this (oldCap 0, newLen 1) point — one triple, not the whole envelope (the slices/append-spill-* pins cover the escaping regimes). Width bound: appendSpillWidth 0 1 = 32 — width 32 >= 32
